content.title: About
content.content: Dried egg white is a dehydrated product made from the whites of chicken eggs. After drying it becomes a light, powdery substance with a pale yellow hue, retaining almost all of the original protein’s nutrients.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Dried egg white is a staple in sports nutrition because of its high protein and low fat content.
It can be stored for 2–3 years when kept in a cool, dry place.
The powder dissolves easily in water, milk, or juice, forming a smooth drink.
It is often added to baked goods to boost protein without altering flavor.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: Dried egg white provides about 80 % protein, making it an excellent source of essential amino acids for muscle recovery.

items.title: Low fat and carbohydrate levels
items.content: Practically free of fats and carbs, it suits low‑carb dietary plans.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Contains riboflavin (B2) and niacin (B3), which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports immune function
items.content: Protein and selenium in the product help maintain a healthy immune system.

items.title: Easily digestible
items.content: The lack of fat makes it quickly digested and absorbed.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Individuals allergic to eggs may experience reactions when consuming dried egg white.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some brands add salt; those monitoring sodium intake should check the label.

items.title: Loss of some micronutrients
items.content: During drying, certain vitamins (e.g., vitamin D) can degrade.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Mix the powder with water, milk, juice, or add it to smoothies. It is commonly used in protein shakes, baking, pancakes, and egg‑free omelets.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep in a sealed container in a dry, cool, dark place. For extended storage, refrigerate to prevent moisture absorption.
